items.title: "The Best Place to Trade on Earth" – Nick Ducoff, Solana Foundation Head of Institutional Growth
items.summary: Nick Ducoff says we're in a "tokenization super cycle." On Solana it runs from a $1 billion BlackRock fund down to an asset worth $50: "So I think we're in a tokenization super cycle. And when you look at the adoption broadly across blockchain, we're over $30B of real world assets, $250B+ of stablecoins. Solana's number two or three in both of those categories, approaching 5 billion in real world assets. And it's a very long tail. There's actually 3,000 different tokenized assets on Solana today. We just hit that threshold the other day, at least as measured by rwa.xyz. And the largest asset on Solana, which is BlackRock's BUIDL Money Fund has a billion dollars in it. And then all the way at the other end of the tail, there's some esoteric asset with 50 bucks. But I think that's the exciting thing, because our vision is really to connect all people with internet access to all valuable assets on the planet." — Nick Ducoff, Head of Institutional Growth Solana Foundation on @TheRollupCo with Robbie Klages

items.title: Solana: Every Asset In Every Market In A Single Place | Vibhu Norby from the Solana Foundation
items.summary: Solana is the Netflix of finance: "Instead of aggregating the supply of book creators or movie producers, it's kind of aggregating the asset issuers, bringing them all into one place, making them all work together. And this leads to kind of network effects that can be pretty strong. And so we call it Vision of Solana One Marketplace, where every asset and every market live together in a single place." — Vibhu Norby, Chief Product Officer of the Solana Foundation, at the @StanfordBlockchainClub's Blockchain Application Stanford Summit (BASS)

items.title: Show HN: ChainBounty – improving the blockchain funding model
items.summary: Abstract. Token-funded bounties to incentivize competition-style participation in blockchain development projects would result in wider and better allocation of investment, and allow investors to diversify exposure across a field of potentially successful projects. Overall this would increase the rate of progress within development of the blockchain space. We propose a centralised platform for the administration of token-funded bounty driven development projects whereby experts allocate pools of invested capital according to the technical merits of development projects, and investors are rewarded with token allocation in funded projects. Draft Whitepaper: http://chainbounty.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/chainbount... We see this as bringing a variation of the YC model to blockchain - experts select large numbers of small projects and provide them with funding to reach the next level of development. This is in contrast to heavily funded ICOs where tiny teams of developers are given hundreds of millions of dollars. After feedback from HN readers: - Do you think this model will better incentivize development in the blockchain space? - What particular challenges do you think would be useful to run? https://twitter.com/ChainBounty/ https://www.facebook.com/ChainBounty-449553402088106/
